chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Abd Allah ibn Jabala, from Is-haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), in a case of
when a slave married a free woman, the child is attached to the free woman; and when a free man married a slave woman, the child is attached to the father.
ai.seo_question: Who does the child follow in status when a slave marries a free person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfarayini’s chain in *al-Istibsar* articulates the principle of *talhq al-walad bi-l-hurr*, ensuring that children of mixed-status unions inherit the liberty of their free parent, thereby preventing the perpetuation of slavery within the family line. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on social mobility and the dignity of the free parent, distinguishing it from other schools that may prioritize the father's status regardless of freedom. The ruling underscores the legal mechanism by which a child’s status is determined at birth based on the higher social standing of the parents.
